title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents

details.title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents
details.abstract: Can simulated shoppers faithfully reproduce real users’ behavior over long shopping interactions? We introduce UserArena , an interactive benchmark grounded in real-world e-commerce data: 64,729 sessions from 11,010 users , covering 566,102 items and 13 action types. Its five-level evaluation goes beyond next-action accuracy to assess sequential behavior, personalization, and outcomes. It also validates offline policy comparisons against a controlled production A/B test. We further propose On-Policy Trajectory Distillation (OPTD) , which uses trajectory-level intent to guide dense token-level teacher supervision on student-generated responses. Among the evaluated simulators, OPTD achieves the strongest overall fidelity and most closely reproduces the policy effect observed in production. 💻 Code & data: https://github.com/RecGPT-Team/UserArena 🌐 Project: https://recgpt-team.github.io/UserArena-Page

title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games

details.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
details.abstract: 🚀 We are excited to share our latest work: "HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games" ! Can an AI agent autonomously complete long-horizon tasks in Minecraft using only visual observations and native keyboard-and-mouse controls, just like a human player? Existing Minecraft agents typically focus on either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy or high-level planning that relies on environment APIs and predefined skills. To this end, we introduce HiSTEVE 1.0 , a hierarchical Vision-Language-Action (VLA) agent that integrates a capability-aware agent harness with a native-control VLA policy, enabling autonomous planning and execution in Minecraft without privileged game states or environment APIs. 🔑 Key Highlights 🧠 Capability-Aware Agent Harness: We develop a hierarchical orchestration framework that combines capability-constrained planning, structured memory, and evidence-driven execution recovery. A policy-coupled task completion detector further enables the agent to determine when to advance, recover, or replan during long-horizon execution. 🎮 Reliable Native-Interface Control: We design a VLA policy that handles both first-person gameplay and GUI interactions through native keyboard-and-mouse actions. To mitigate interference between these heterogeneous interaction regimes, we introduce regime-specific RMSNorm branches and separate mouse-movement token embeddings, together with a three-stage training strategy combining world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning. 📈 Extensive Experimental Validation: HiSTEVE achieves state-of-the-art atomic-task performance, reaching 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and 37.4% average success on OpenHA. The complete agent also successfully executes long-horizon tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch using only the human interface. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31162 We welcome feedback and discussions!

title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods

RSIHub lets researchers compose reusable operators to improve agent prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration, while keeping evaluation protected and candidate histories traceable. We implement AHE, Hyperagents, A-Evolve, and GEPA on shared infrastructure and evaluate them with MiniSWE and Codex on Terminal Bench 2 and τ³ Banking. Our goal is to make agent self-improvement experiments easier to reproduce, compare, and extend. title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain

details.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
details.abstract: Introduction We present RynnUnify , a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture with an autoregressive Reasoner and a rectified-flow video Generator . Built on Cosmos3, RynnUnify connects embodied understanding, spatial grounding, and long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video-language reasoning. Unified Embodied Brain. RynnUnify brings embodied cognition, spatial grounding, and video generation into one architecture, connecting scene understanding with predictions of how the physical world evolves. Interleaved Visual Planning. RynnUnify alternates subtask reasoning with video prediction, using each generated outcome to plan the next step. Cross-chunk scene memory, self-forcing training, and adaptive durations support coherent visual planning over long horizons. Agentic Interleaved Thinking. An RL-trained agent learns when to answer directly and when to generate visual evidence. Through BCPO, it learns to formulate generation requests, interpret predicted outcomes, and select the reasoning path that benefits the task. Connect Prediction to Action. The World-Action Model ( WAM ) extension translates predictive world representations into robot control through joint video-action training, supporting composite manipulation tasks.

title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions

details.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
details.abstract: We introduce state trees , a new representation in which every weight is a path of discrete decisions, and decisions can be shared across weights. Quantization, pruning, low-rank factorization and weight sharing all become edits on a tree, and applying the weights reduces to shifts and additions. We hope it opens new directions in compression, efficient kernels and hardware. As a first, deliberately simple application, we build a state tree on the original weights, one node per 64 values. Every weight and every KV-cache value still decodes to its exact BF16 bits directly on the tensorcores , with no calibration and no accuracy trade-off. On Qwen3-8B (A100, vLLM): 24% fewer bits for the weights (12.1 instead of 16) and 22% for the KV cache up to 1.28× faster generation, end to end 1.49× more tokens in the KV cache at the same memory budget decode attention 1.2–2.5× faster than FlashAttention-2 on the same values

title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models

details.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
details.abstract: Can a language model improve itself without a single human-written question or answer? We introduce On-Policy Self-Training (OPST), which reformulates on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. Guided only by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model builds its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces, with no human-curated prompts or answers. A pseudo-verification filter keeps a problem only if the model can reproduce its answer in a fresh context and under a paraphrase. We evaluate in-domain self-improvement as well as knowledge retention on out-of-domain benchmarks when mixing generation domains, and transfer to multimodal inputs with Visual OPST. OPST improves both language and multimodal reasoning without human-curated questions or answers, and outperforms alternative training strategies.

title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation

details.title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation
details.abstract: The rapid growth of microdramas has increased demand for high-quality script production. Long-form microdrama script generation with LLMs requires both diverse plot progression and long-range narrative coherence. Our observations reveal that candidate continuations increasingly concentrate on fewer narrative mechanisms as generation progresses, while conventional retrieval may reinforce trope reuse and overlook historical information essential to future plots. To address these challenges, we propose DraMaze, a multi-agent pipeline that explores diverse causal paths through trope memory-guided evolutionary tree search and mutation. It further constructs a Backward Narrative Dependency Tree to organize, retain, and retrieve historical memories based on future narrative goals. We also introduce MiDramaBench, a bilingual benchmark for evaluating script logic and creative quality across different script lengths, together with causal-pattern metrics for narrative repetition and diversity. Experiments show consistent improvements across three backbone LLMs. For 60-episode scripts of up to 60k words, DraMaze reduces causal-pattern repetition by 32.1% and achieves a Logic score of 82.5, outperforming the best-performing baseline by 8.5 points.

title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching

details.title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching
details.abstract: FLOMSS systematically investigates flow matching for full-band stereo music source separation (MSS). Systematic design study: We investigate prediction targets, flow paths, single- vs. multi-source modeling, and mixture consistency. Optimal Transport-CFM with x-prediction provides the most balanced performance across the evaluated metrics. Beyond SDR: We evaluate MSS with signal-level, spectral, embedding-based, distributional, and subjective metrics, revealing a distributional–reconstruction trade-off: flow-matching models improve spectral and embedding-based similarity while generally sacrificing some SDR. Strong generative MSS performance: FLOMSS-S outperforms prior generative baselines on most spectral and perceptual metrics. Competitive subjective quality: Scaling to FLOMSS-M improves every reported objective metric over FLOMSS-S and ranks #2 overall in the listening test, despite its lower SDR than strong discriminative separators. These results highlight flow matching as a promising direction for generative music source separation with competitive perceptual quality.

title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation

details.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
details.abstract: ✨ Highlights Role-specific learning signals — MultiAgent-OPD combines local process supervision for Searchers with outcome-based reinforcement learning for the Leader and Answerer, addressing credit assignment in hierarchical multi-agent teams. Two-stage training recipe — First trains a teacher to search and summarize in a cascaded Search–Answer workflow, then transfers its expertise to Searchers during joint hierarchical training. Token-level on-policy distillation — A frozen, task-trained teacher scores student-generated queries and summaries on evolving subtask trajectories, providing fine-grained guidance for evidence acquisition and reporting. Joint training with a shared model — Leader, Searcher, and Answerer roles jointly optimize a shared language model to coordinate task decomposition, multi-wave search, and answer generation. Inference requires only the trained student. Strong performance across seven QA benchmarks — MultiAgent-OPD achieves 38.68% macro avg@4, outperforming M-GRPO like LLM Judge MAS-RL method by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL (cascaded MAS-RL method) by 2.61 points at the evaluated checkpoints.

title: MMVistaReason: Toward Open-Data and Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Reasoning

details.title: MMVistaReason: Toward Open-Data and Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Reasoning
details.abstract: Open multimodal reasoning models have benefited from large-scale reasoning supervision, yet reliable post-training remains challenging due to uneven data quality, inefficient supervision construction, imbalanced difficulty, and cross-domain interference. We introduce MMVistaReason (MVR), an open-data post-training recipe with three components: (1) broader capability coverage across complementary Analytical and Real-World reasoning groups, emphasizing structured reasoning versus visual perception and spatial grounding; (2) efficient SFT and RL data construction, standardizing heterogeneous open data through staged cleaning and annotation, combining difficulty-aware cascaded teacher distillation with answer-likelihood-based trajectory selection to construct MVR-SFT-528K, and applying scale-specific frontier filtering for MVR-RL-63K; and (3) specialize-then-integrate training, which trains complementary RL experts and consolidates their capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Our analyses reveal a capacity-dependent interaction between supervision difficulty, trajectory quality, and model capacity: smaller students benefit more from selected supervision, while larger students are robust to trajectory variation and mixed-domain interference. Mixed-domain RL introduces benchmark-level negative transfer, whereas MOPD provides consistent capability integration, with the preferred KL direction varying across model scales. Across 15 multimodal benchmarks, MVR-4B achieves an average score of 72.8, outperforming Qwen3.5-9B (Instruct) and MMFineReason-8B while using about 70% fewer samples than MMFineReason. Scaling to 9B improves the average to 74.4, surpassing Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (Instruct). Overall, MMVistaReason demonstrates that systematic open-data construction and capacity-aware post-training provide a practical and scalable path toward reliable multimodal reasoning.

title: DuoLM: Fast and Effective Personalized Recommendation with Language Models

details.title: DuoLM: Fast and Effective Personalized Recommendation with Language Models
details.abstract: Introducing DuoLM DuoLM is a framework for fast, personalized recommendation with two jointly trained language models. An encoder turns item descriptions into compact representations that can be cached and reused across users. A ranker combines these representations with each user’s history and feedback to make personalized recommendations. Both models learn end to end from recommendation labels and guidance from a full-text teacher. The serving runtime makes this reuse practical: item representations stay on the GPU and are accessed through virtual token IDs, multiple candidates share history computation within each request, and CUDA Graphs reduce execution overhead. Together, the model and runtime reduce repeated work throughout the recommendation process.

title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders

details.title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders
details.abstract: 🌍 LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders Location encoders such as SatCLIP and GeoCLIP turn (lat, lon) into general-purpose embeddings by contrastive alignment with satellite imagery. This paper shows why this works and what it takes to make it multimodal. Key findings 📐 Location encoders provably keep contrastive learning away from its optimum, and training image and location encoders jointly from scratch collapses the embedding covariance to very low rank. 🔁 SatCLIP-style encoders work because the frozen image encoder acts as a high-rank covariance regularizer that the location encoder folds onto. 🛰️ Extending this to multiple sensors requires a target that is co-aligned across modalities and has high effective rank. LoCA (Location Contrastive Alignment) Stage 1: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 encoders are co-aligned with contrastive learning. Stage 2: location and metadata encoders are fitted onto them with multi-view contrastive learning. At inference, only coordinates are needed. Results: against SatCLIP, GeoCLIP, GT-Loc, AlphaEarth and Copernicus-FM on 17 tasks (land cover, wildfire, climate, geophysical, socio-economic, biodiversity), LoCA has the most task wins, ranks top-2 on 11, and wins 68.8% of pairwise comparisons against the other encoders. Its embeddings use 62% of their dimensions, compared with 35% for SatCLIP. 💻 Code and pretrained weights (coming soon): https://github.com/eleannavali/LoCA

title: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models

details.title: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models
details.abstract: Recognizing task completion and failure enables robots to stop upon success and initiate recovery or replanning after failure. Existing methods augment Vision Language Action (VLA) policies with task status signal prediction to support these execution decisions. However, learning and integrating these signals can require fine-grained supervision, external monitoring models, or complex architectural designs. Moreover, the potential of task status signals to directly guide action generation remains underexplored. We present Echo, a framework that combines task status signal learning without frame-level progress annotations with a compact design for status prediction and action generation within a single VLA. Specifically, Echo represents task status with stop and failure signals, added as two dimensions of each action chunk and denoised together with robot actions. Their combination distinguishes ongoing execution, successful completion, and failure. To learn these signals without fine-grained progress annotations, Echo constructs successful, failed, and recovery trajectories with complementary supervision properties. To enable status signal-guided action generation, Echo controls interactions between the signals and actions and denoises the signals faster than the actions. These allow later action denoising steps to condition on cleaner status estimates while preserving accurate signal prediction. Extensive real-world manipulation experiments show that Echo accurately predicts task status and consistently improves policy performance.

title: A path-following framework on fiber bundle for variational inequalities

details.title: A path-following framework on fiber bundle for variational inequalities
details.abstract: This paper presents a general-purpose path-following algorithm that solves general variational inequalities with continuous mappings and polytope domains to arbitrary precision, achieving global linear convergence: exact for nonsingular solutions, and up to any prescribed precision for singular ones. The key insight is to view the solution set of a fixed-point KKT system as a fiber bundle (the "fixed-point bundle") over the simplex, whose geometry separates motion along the base from motion along the fibers. This unifies starting point selection, path-following, and singularity avoidance: at a singular point, where existing path-following guarantees break down, the algorithm simply jumps along the fiber to a nonsingular point and continues. Experiments on 6400 random instances with dimensions up to 1024 reduce the gap below 1e-5 in every case; code and data are available at https://github.com/shb20tsinghua/FiberBundle_VI . A follow-up (arXiv:2609.16158) extends the framework to product-of-simplex domains for Nash equilibrium computation.

title: The fixed-point bundle method over product-of-simplex domains arising from game equilibria

details.title: The fixed-point bundle method over product-of-simplex domains arising from game equilibria
details.abstract: This paper extends the fiber-bundle path-following framework of arXiv:2606.00778 to product-of-simplex domains, so that the algorithm solves arbitrary m-player n-action general-sum games to arbitrary precision, inheriting global linear convergence: exact for nonsingular equilibria, and up to any prescribed precision for singular ones. Rather than re-proving convergence, we construct an equivalent variational inequality on a single simplex and establish a fiber bundle isomorphism between the two frameworks, complemented by a slice-extension argument that transfers all guarantees from the original paper. The resulting composite bundle also permits jumps along fibers that avoid singular points, where existing path-following guarantees would otherwise break down. Experiments on 5600 random instances with dimensions ranging from 2-player 128-action to 128-player 2-action reduce the gap below 1e-5 in every case; code and data are available at https://github.com/shb20tsinghua/FiberBundle_VI .

title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent

details.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
details.abstract: Vision-language models are shifting from offline passive understanding toward online proactive interaction. However, prevailing methods largely rely on explicit requests while overlooking implicit user intents (e.g., “where should I click next?” when a user is navigating a website) and fail to continuously update their understanding as user intents evolve. These limitations make them less suitable for intent-aware interaction in real-world scenarios. To address these challenges, we introduce StreamVibe-Bench, a new benchmark that serves as a testbed for user intent understanding and interaction, comprising 4.1K evaluation samples and 85K training samples spanning explicit, implicit, and dynamic intents. Building on this benchmark, we develop StreamVibe-VL, a streaming proactive model that infers implicit user intents from continuous observations and dynamically adapts its interactions as these intents evolve. We further introduce StreamVibe-Harness, which maintains user intents as persistent states with flexible lifecycles through hierarchical memory, enabling it to track the latest user intents and environmental states. Our experiments reveal three key findings: (i) StreamVibe-VL preserves strong general video understanding capabilities while improving response timing and answer quality by 10.7% over existing baselines; (ii) existing proactive models remain limited in understanding user intents and determining when to respond, especially under implicit and dynamic intents; and (iii) StreamVibe-Harness further improves response consistency and adaptation during sustained interactions, resulting in a 12.3% gain in proactive interaction performance.

details.title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
details.abstract: Task success does not always mean the agent harness worked reliably. We introduce TraceTrial-Bench, a benchmark that evaluates agent task performance and harness reliability separately, using 95 mechanism-oriented tasks across seven components: context, execution, governance, lifecycle, observability, tools, and verification. Across 4 harnesses, 9 models, and 3,420 runs, 31.1% of runs achieve task success despite failing at least one harness criterion. Our framework combines trajectory tracing, multi-source evidence, and two-layer evaluation to support auditable reliability assessment and evidence-based failure analysis. title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization

details.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
details.abstract: As foundation models evolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. However, existing research lacks a unified perspective on how agents reliably accomplish delegated work. To address this gap, we present a work-centric, system-level perspective that views work agents as systems combining foundation models and runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful workspaces and deliver verifiable outcomes. We introduce two complementary dimensions, work persistence and work openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task scope and organization. Building on this framework, we identify five core capability families required for reliable work execution and examine approaches to model optimization, harness optimization, and their joint optimization. We further analyze existing evaluation methods and metrics from the perspective of work outcomes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including sustained work delegation, adaptation to open environments, and the interaction between work execution and capability improvement. This paper provides a unified framework for understanding, optimizing, and evaluating work agents, supporting the development of systems capable of delivering reliable, verifiable, and practically valuable work outcomes.

title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL

details.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
details.abstract: Rubric-based rewards enable effective reinforcement learning on non-verifiable tasks. However, because these rewards are typically defined as a weighted measure of rubric coverage, models are trained primarily to maximize a recall objective. As a result, RL-trained models produce responses that are more complete but also more verbose and contain more unnecessary or factually incorrect content, leading them to be less preferred than responses from the base model. To address this issue, we present the FORK reward, which jointly optimizes recall and a novel precision objective, which requires each unit of a model response to be both necessary and factually correct, as measured by rubric-driven necessity credits and a factual-correctness grader, respectively. Our experimental results show that FORK outperforms existing rubric-based RL methods and achieves Pareto-optimal performance that balances rubric coverage and overall response quality. Compared to the original recall-based reward, FORK substantially improves precision and reduces response length while achieving similar rubric coverage, which leads to significantly higher win rate compared to the base policy (e.g., from 10.6% to 68.0% on RubricHub-Medical and from 22.1% to 74.1% on HealthBench).

title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges

details.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
details.abstract: AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) extends this process to inductive biases and to the mechanisms that govern future updates, which can themselves be revised and reused across improvement cycles. Yet self-modification alone does not guarantee trustworthy improvement. Reported gains may reflect flawed evaluations, previously acquired capabilities may deteriorate, and compliance with behavioral constraints may weaken. Compromised artifacts or sensitive information may also persist in successor systems. Changes to improvement mechanisms may invalidate earlier verification results and make human oversight less effective. This survey presents an operational definition and process framework for RSI and organizes the requirements for trustworthy RSI into four interconnected themes: genuine and sustained improvement; behavioral constraints, alignment, and fairness; system security and privacy; and transparency and controllability. We examine these themes from three perspectives: Improvement Validity, Constraint Preservation, and Effective Oversight. This analysis covers improvement diagnosis, proposal generation, proposal evaluation, and update implementation (S1--S4), including the recursive application of these stages to improvement mechanisms (RI). We review risks, safeguards, and evaluation evidence for individual updates, effects inherited by successor systems, and revisions to improvement mechanisms, while distinguishing direct RSI findings from evidence in related systems. Finally, we examine evaluation settings, identify requirements for independent and longitudinal assessment, and discuss applications and open research problems.

details.abstract: 🚀 Introducing Continual Learning Exam (CLE): Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents! 🧠 Can LLM agents truly learn from experience and continuously improve over time? Most existing agent benchmarks focus on whether agents can solve individual tasks. But real-world intelligence requires more than task completion: agents should learn from past successes and failures, accumulate experience, and transfer acquired knowledge, strategies, and skills to future challenges. To bridge this gap, we introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate long-horizon continual learning and experience-driven self-improvement in LLM agents. 🌟 Key Highlights: 🔹 Built with 50+ domain experts, covering 120 real-world professional tasks, 600 progressive levels, and 89 occupations across 12 domains. 🔹 Realistic professional environments, featuring ~24K real-world files, 19 stateful applications, and 16K+ human-authored evaluation criteria. 🔹 Game-like Task Ladders, where agents must complete each level to unlock the next. Later levels require agents to reuse and build upon knowledge, strategies, and skills acquired through earlier experience. 📊 Key Findings: We evaluated 17 frontier agent configurations. Even the strongest system, Claude Code + Opus 5, achieves only: • 47.7% level completion rate • 23.3% full Task Ladder completion rate These results reveal a substantial gap between solving individual tasks and achieving genuine long-term continual learning. We hope CLE can serve as a realistic and verifiable benchmark to advance research on Agent Continual Learning, Memory, Skill Learning, and Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI). 💡 Beyond Task Solving: Towards Continual Learning and Experience-Driven Self-Improvement. title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning

details.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
details.abstract: Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training. Common alternatives lack token-level credit assignment and typically rely on grouped rollouts to estimate prompt-specific baselines. A critic can address both limitations, but longCoT critic training is hindered by insufficient coverage of trajectories with diverse lengths and early gradients dominated by the newly initialized value head. We introduce S3AC (Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor–Critic) for LLM reasoning, built around a practical critictraining recipe. The trained critic provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines. Using the prompt-level baseline to estimate difficulty, we propose DifficultyAware Prompt Sampling (DAPS). DAPS combines this estimate with outcome history to select prompts before generation, reducing rollout waste without offline difficulty initialization. S3AC improves group-rollout performance across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, outperforming a modern GRPO variant (GRPO-X). At 35B, it sustains single-rollout training while tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.

Based on such insights, we propose ``ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning''.   It calibrates the GRPO-type credit assignment and results in the improvement of effectiveness and efficiency under multiple setups.

title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning

details.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
details.abstract: 🚀 Can we really train LLMs with native FP4 reinforcement learning — without sacrificing stability? Excited to share miniTE , our open-source framework for stable and efficient native NVFP4 (W4A4) RL! One surprising finding: Same weights + same precision ≠ same policy. Even when both the learner and rollout engine use NVFP4, subtle differences in numerical execution can introduce significant training–inference mismatch and eventually destabilize RL. With miniTE, we tackle this challenge from both numerical and systems perspectives: 🔬 Diagnose & align: Identify cross-engine execution differences and bring training–inference log-probability gaps down to ~1e-8 in our strict-alignment setting. ⚡ Make FP4 actually fast: Optimize native NVFP4 kernels, scaling, and grouped GEMMs, achieving up to 1.39× BF16 learner throughput on 8×B300 GPUs. 📈 Keep learning stable: Demonstrate long-horizon RL on Qwen3-30B-A3B with downstream performance close to BF16. Beyond the results, we're releasing the framework, kernels, diagnostics, and training recipes to make native low-bit RL easier to reproduce and extend. FP4 is not just about using fewer bits — it's about making every bit work. 🔥 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23928 💻 Details: https://infix.io/research/miniTE We'd love to hear your thoughts, feedback, and ideas for pushing low-precision RL further!

title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization

details.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization
details.abstract: Recent work shows that increasing embedding capacity can improve language models, making it a promising direction for scaling. As more capacity goes into embedding tables, extreme compression becomes increasingly important: we want to keep the benefits of larger embeddings while fitting models into limited deployment memory. We study this in Gemma 4, where per-layer embeddings (PLE) account for 35.2% of E4B's parameters. At 100× compression, only about five bytes remain for each token–layer vector. Encoding every vector independently gives each one a tiny code and misses the opportunity to share storage across layers. Our method, OPTIC, gives each token one quantized code shared across all layers. Layer-specific affine decoders reconstruct the different PLE vectors from that shared code. We also fit the representation to its effect after the gate and output projection, so the compression objective reflects how the model actually uses the embeddings. At about 100× PLE compression, OPTIC retains 97.8% of BF16 E4B performance across seven benchmarks, compared with 66.3% for product quantization. Serving BF16 E4B directly from the compact codes reduces GPU memory by 29.7%, with at most 0.40% more wall time on an RTX 4090 with the same 1 GiB KV cache. It also works alongside backbone weight quantization. Paper · Code and method walkthrough · Released 100× PLE artifact

title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion

details.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
details.abstract: Diffusion-based video generation models (VGMs) can synthesize visually compelling content, but maintaining geometrically consistent camera ego-motion across frames remains an open problem. Camera ego-motion describes these cross-frame viewpoint changes; geometrically inconsistent future predictions can induce systematic errors in downstream action prediction. To address this problem, we propose CausalAlign, a framework combining causal diagnosis and delta-token alignment. First, we diagnose how ego-motion is represented, used, and retained within VGMs using linear probes and causal interventions. In the base model, both measures rise and then fall across denoising layers and timesteps: ego-motion is used at intermediate stages but is not retained later, a pattern we call geometric state forgetting. Second, we construct a delta-token space from a 3D foundation model and align VGM representations where ego-motion begins to fade. Delta tokens encode changes between consecutive frames, focusing supervision on motion rather than redundant static scene content. With Wan2.2 fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, CausalAlign preserves visual quality while improving motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness. For example, it reduces geometric consistency errors by more than 20% relative to the base model. Moreover, using the fine-tuned VGM, CausalAlign improves downstream world action models (WAMs) on the RoboCasa365 benchmark. Overall, CausalAlign improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields gains in downstream embodied models on motion-intensive tasks.

title: Joint or Per-Option? Compact Encoders for Closed-Set Decisions from 17 Million to 1 Billion Parameters

details.abstract: Author here. Many LM pipelines end in a closed-set decision: pick a tool, a label, a route. We asked two things: how small an encoder for this can be, and whether it should read the options jointly or one at a time. Per-option vs joint: in a three-seed study at 32M parameters, per-option scoring wins by 5.8 points of chance-corrected skill at matched optimizer steps, and by 2.8 at roughly matched compute. The advantage needs a reranker initialisation; from the raw encoder the two readers are indistinguishable. Cost: per-option needs 5–13× more encoder passes, so joint is what we released. Released models: six open joint encoders, from 17M to 1B. On 209 overlap-audited System1-Arena tasks, the 68M and 150M beat a 435M DeBERTa-v3 zero-shot classifier by 4.9 and 5.9 accuracy points. On the 145 tasks unseen in training they are at least on par with it. Latency: the 17M answers a median request in 14 ms on 16 CPU threads. A caveat we measured: reordering options changes 12–23% of the joint models' answers. title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents

details.title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents
details.abstract: Language model agents often abandon correct work when a user challenges it, yet simply telling them to stand firm makes them ignore real mistakes. Once an agent reads a complaint, it tends to discount its own earlier checks in order to agree with the user. We introduce Thinking-in-Bets, a training-free method in which an agent writes a short private record of its main claims, the checks supporting them, and its confidence before reading user feedback. When challenged, the agent consults this Claim Checklist to keep verified work intact while investigating uncertain or newly challenged parts. We evaluate five Gemini models (3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.5 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.8 Flash, and 4.0 Argon) across eight benchmarks: SWE-Together, SWE-Interact, and DeepSWE for software engineering, Agents' Last Exam for professional reports, Humanity's Last Exam and SycEval for academic reasoning, Vals Finance for financial analysis, and Terminal-Bench for command-line tasks. Recording claims before criticism nearly eliminates false reversals in patch review and protects passing report drafts under mistaken pushback, whereas writing the same record after reading the complaint recovers very little of the gain. In multi-turn coding, pre-reply claim records substantially reduce unnecessary file edits after mistaken complaints, and gating the record so it is written only when the agent is uncertain lowers token overhead while fixing more real bugs than the baseline. Even in non-interactive tasks without user feedback, listing the key claims in a draft and re-checking the weakest one before submission improves both answer accuracy and confidence estimates across all tested models.

It's polite, fluent and never says anything false... and twenty turns later you still don't have your forecast. 🌦️ That's procedural hallucination : the agent stops following the procedure it was given. Every turn looks fine on its own, so fact-checkers and per-turn quality metrics miss it. DialFork is a benchmark for catching it, with no annotation needed. We take a conversation where the agent does everything right, replay it with the same seed, and slip the agent a new instruction at some point, so the conversation "forks" 🔱. The fork position gives us labels for free: how far each fork strays and the turn where it starts straying. 36,278 English dialogues · 24 tasks · 12 domains · 4 hallucination types 3 tasks: set-to-set distance (monitoring), dialog-to-dialog distance (procedural retrieval) and turn prediction (real-time guardrails) 🤗 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/DialFork/dialfork 💻 Code & leaderboard: https://github.com/idiap/dialfork

details.title: Trust Mechanisms for Offline Generative AI at the Edge: A Connectivity-Regime Framework and an Empirical Study on a Raspberry Pi 5

Key findings: A calibrated retrieval-score gate detects out-of-corpus queries almost perfectly (AUROC 0.97) but in-topic unanswerable questions poorly (0.68). A simple deterministic output validator turns malformed outputs into explicit abstentions at no observed cost in correct answers. Signature and hash checks alone accepted 6 of 9 update attacks (rollback, replay, expiry, revoked keys, model incompatibility); layered verification rejected all 9 in about 4.5 ms. A validly signed but poisoned knowledge pack passed every check and eliminated correct answers on all 30 targets: integrity establishes provenance, not truth. details.abstract: Can frontier AI models generate CAD models that are actually usable in engineering? Unlike evaluations centered on simplified or toy examples, our study assesses GPT-6 Astra using realistic engineering CAD models with nontrivial complexity. More importantly, we evaluate not only whether AI can generate CAD geometry, but also whether the resulting models satisfy multiple engineering usability requirements, including geometric validity, functional completeness, assembly feasibility, and parametric editability. Across CAD understanding, generation, editing, and evaluation tasks, our findings reveal an important transition: general-purpose AI models are beginning to demonstrate practical value in engineering design, while significant challenges remain in ensuring engineering reliability. The key question is no longer just whether AI can create CAD models, but whether those models can actually be used in engineering workflows. The goal is not to declare a winning model, but to understand where smaller models are genuinely useful, where they struggle, and what it takes to make them effective in real development environments. title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence

details.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
details.abstract: ChronoReplay is a training framework designed to improve the spatial reasoning capabilities of streaming vision-language models (VLMs). Existing spatial VLMs often specialize in specific answer formats, such as categorical spatial relations, metric distances, or motion trajectories. This specialization, which we call interface lock-in, limits generalization across different spatial reasoning tasks. To address this challenge, ChronoReplay organizes heterogeneous spatial supervision into chronologically ordered episodes, preserves task-specific answer formats, and balances learning across supervision families. This enables a single model to learn complementary spatial capabilities while maintaining temporal consistency. Key Highlights: Unified Spatial Learning: Supports categorical, metric, and trajectory-based spatial reasoning within a single model. Chronological Replay: Preserves temporal dependencies by organizing training examples into ordered interaction episodes. Family-Balanced Training: Improves cross-task generalization by balancing heterogeneous supervision signals. Strong Benchmark Performance: Achieves consistent improvements across OVO-S-Bench, OST-Bench, and UCS-Bench, including a 13.41-point improvement on OST-Bench. Efficient Streaming Inference: Adaptive frame selection further improves performance while reducing visual processing costs. ChronoReplay demonstrates that effective streaming spatial intelligence requires preserving complementary spatial information across tasks, learning from temporally structured experiences, and selecting relevant visual evidence at inference time.

title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?

details.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
details.abstract: Video captioning aims to preserve visual information through compact descriptions, predominantly using natural language. However, precisely expressing fine-grained spatial structures and temporal dynamics in natural language often leads to lengthy and potentially ambiguous descriptions. In this work, we explore Code as Video Caption, a paradigm where executable programs serve as a complementary representation of visual content through graphical primitives, layout rules, and functions of time. To examine whether code captions effectively preserve video information, we compare them with natural language captions on downstream question answering and video reconstruction tasks. Our results show that code captions achieve superior reasoning accuracy and reconstruction fidelity. Despite these advantages, realizing the potential of code captioning depends on whether current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate faithful code captions. To systematically assess this capability, we introduce CodeCap-Bench, which comprises 323 videos spanning five categories of structured 2D content, along with fine-grained annotations and a multi-level evaluation framework. Extensive experiments reveal that while leading proprietary MLLMs demonstrate promising code captioning capabilities, they still struggle to faithfully capture complex temporal dynamics, with open-source models lagging substantially behind.

title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?

details.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
details.abstract: This paper investigates whether discrete visual tokens can preserve semantic information as effectively as continuous representations. It shows that reconstruction error is an unreliable indicator of multimodal understanding and identifies effective bit budget as a key performance factor. The proposed Factorized Vector Quantization (FVQ) uses complementary, fixed-dimensional projections and parallel codebooks to overcome performance saturation in existing quantizers. Experiments demonstrate that FVQ scales effectively with increasing bit budgets and matches continuous features in controlled evaluations. At industrial scale, FVQ achieves strong multimodal understanding, including fine-grained OCR, challenging the assumption that visual discretization necessarily entails semantic degradation in downstream understanding tasks.

title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning

details.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
details.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld , a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the intermediate dynamics connecting the current world to a future state and serves as a common action representation across embodiments. We first initialize CoD with action-labeled demonstrations, then predict the future induced by each CoD and reinforce those whose predictions better match the observed outcome. This enables videos without action annotations to provide direct supervision from observed state transitions, allowing human and robot experience to refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate effective human-to-robot transfer and strong generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?

details.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
details.abstract: Recent test-time training (TTT) frameworks have enabled open-weight large language models (LLMs) to outperform inference-only frameworks powered by frontier models on scientific discovery tasks. However, TTT introduces additional computational cost for online weight updates during the discovery process, making computational efficiency an important consideration when scaling to larger models. This motivates us to explore an efficient test-time adaptation method for scientific discovery. We introduce Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME), a plug-and-play test-time adaptation method, as an alternative to TTT. TTME continually updates the external memory by distilling the experience to guide subsequent discovery without updating model weights. To have a clean comparison, we evaluate TTME and TTT under the same discovery framework, replacing only the test-time adaptation method.  Our evaluation shows that TTME outperforms TTT on all five mathematical tasks, while reducing computational cost by 82.8-84.6% in FLOPs and 47.7-58.4% in runtime. These results establish TTME as an effective and computationally efficient alternative to TTT in the evaluated discovery settings.

title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation

details.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
details.abstract: 🎬 VibeVideoBench: Can AI agents make a finished video, entirely with code? Agents writing code to make videos is a new way to generate video 💡: multimodal agents write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound, so formulas, charts and narration timed to on-screen events come out exact. Meet VibeVideoBench 🚀, to our knowledge the first benchmark of general multimodal agents on open-domain, code-driven video generation with audio. 📦 The benchmark • 239 self-contained tasks in English and Chinese across 12 categories: data stories, music-driven pieces, classroom lessons, paper explainers, games, build-and-process videos and more • Agents run fully autonomously in their native harness, in a sandbox with no image or video generation model, only TTS • Deliver a finished MP4 with sound within one hour ⏱️ 🔍 Evaluation: hierarchical and evidence-based • L1 program checks of the delivery spec ✅ • L2 ~13k task-specific rubric checks, each traced to the requirement it enforces 📋 • L3 five quality dimensions, anchored per task 🎯 • Three independent VLM judge panels; audio checks only go to judges that can hear 👂 📊 Key findings (9 frontier agent systems, 2,151 scored rollouts) 🥇 GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 rank 1st and 2nd with both the judges and blind human raters 🧩 Far from solved: the best system meets every core requirement on only 76.3% of tasks 📦 Delivery is a second axis: counting missing videos as zero reshuffles the ranking. Gemini 4 Argon delivers 77% of its videos and drops from 4th to 7th ⏰ Of 224 runs with no playable video, 169 are final renders that started too late, ran too slowly or never started. The problem is how agents plan their hour 🛠️ Every system keeps its own rendering stack; 95% of runs inspect their own frames, yet how much they look doesn't predict quality (ρ = −0.07) ⚖️ The judges rank systems like humans do (ρ = 0.98) but agree on only 73% of individual pairs: good for ranking systems, not single videos 🌐 Project page: https://vibevideobench.github.io/

We present Zooming-without-Zooming-v2 (ZwZ2) , a family of 4B/9B/27B models trained to connect evidence through reinforcement learning. Our EvidenceConnect framework uses privileged regional views to synthesize compositional questions, with cross-model agreement and region-ablation checks assessing label reliability and evidence dependence. Trained only on single-image questions and requiring no inference-time zooming, ZwZ2 improves over its base models on all 25 benchmarks across six domains , generalizing to multimodal long-context understanding, embodied spatial reasoning, and agents. We release all three models, the training dataset, and code. title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback

details.title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
details.abstract: Can AI agents autonomously train useful language models and improve them using feedback from users? We introduce RSI Arena, a two-stage study of autonomous post-training as a step toward recursive self-improvement. Ten frontier models act as training agents, each starting from NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base. During a six-day first stage, each agent has 1,000 GPU-hours and $300 in API credit on a shared 64-GPU cluster, independently selecting data, implementing training procedures, and choosing checkpoints. We evaluate their models on 20 benchmarks and through blind human evaluations. All ten agents produce working assistants, with the strongest model, trained by GPT-6 Astra, closing a median of 76% of the base-to-Instruct gap across 12 capability benchmarks. Its human-preference rating is also close to NVIDIA Instruct after statistical adjustment for answer length and formatting. In Stage 2, each agent receives the comparison records and votes involving its Stage 1 model and is given three additional days for further training. Using NVIDIA Instruct as a common reference across the two evaluation rounds, we observe an improvement from Stage 1 to Stage 2 in the style-adjusted relative rating of eight of the ten models. We show that benchmark gains were modest, with no clear link to preference gains, while some agents encouraged longer responses and one model showed increased harmful compliance on StrongREJECT. RSI Arena provides an auditable setting for studying how human feedback can guide autonomous model development. It takes a step toward recursive self-improvement with human feedback (RSIHF), in which people help define what improvement means for the AI systems they use.

details.title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions

We design an action-conditioning mechanism that combines global action tokens with locally identity-initialized, frame-aligned injection, associating transition descriptors with the corresponding future video latents. We enable latent-action-guided generation under edited robot embodiments and environments, and adapt the world model to native robot-action conditioning. The resulting latent-action synthesis and digital-teleoperation pipelines generate data that improves downstream policy learning in the evaluated settings.

title: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents

details.title: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents
details.abstract: Generative models increasingly expose a reasoning effort setting that lets users scale inference-time compute, trading higher cost for potentially improved performance. Users must choose an effort level before knowing whether extra reasoning will help, and even a successful run does not reveal whether the effort purchased was necessary. Reasoning effort is therefore a credence good: buyers observe the outcome but cannot assess the marginal value of the computation they paid for. In this work, we measure the counterfactual effect of effort levels on both proprietary and open-weight models on four benchmarks, spanning single-call reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks. Effort, it turns out, does not consistently preserve tasks that lower effort solves, can overspend, and can change trajectory behavior. First, we find that although higher effort can raise accuracy in aggregate, it frequently fails on tasks that lower effort solved. Second, on the subset of easy tasks that every effort level solves, higher effort is generally more costly, with the highest effort level costing up to 42x as much as the lowest. Lastly, effort changes not only how many tokens are used, but also how agents solve tasks: at higher effort, agents verify their own work more heavily and more often search for solutions than work through problems directly, both of which lengthen trajectories without necessarily altering the outcome. These findings show that naively choosing the highest level is not only cost-inefficient but also offers no guarantee of the best instance-level performance. A simple alternative, starting at the lowest effort and escalating only after a verified failure, matches or improves on fixed top effort across all models and benchmarks at lower cost for most proprietary models.

title: The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data

details.title: The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data
details.abstract: 🎯 What traces does pre-training data leave on a language model? We've just arXived our NeurIPS 2026 paper, The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data! In this work, we explore how pre-training data shapes zero-shot behavior through word-level unigram cross-entropy, a simple, model-free measure of lexical alignment between pre-training corpora and target benchmarks. Perhaps unsurprisingly, we find that nearly all vocabulary in standard benchmarks is already covered during pre-training, given the billions of tokens used to train LLMs. What matters is not simply which words a model has seen, but how probability mass is distributed across them. This distribution leaves a measurable lexical imprint on the model's predictive behavior. Across controlled from-scratch experiments, we find that stronger lexical alignment consistently tracks higher zero-shot accuracy. #NeurIPS2026 #Pretraining #LLM #NAVER #KAIST_AI

title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction

details.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
details.abstract: Diffusion LMs already know most of the next tokens. What they miss is the order. SPOT learns it. Exact decoding of a diffusion LM fills one masked position per pass. The model's predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at over 90% of positions, but not which position comes next. SPOT is a 0.62M-parameter drafter that predicts this order from the target's own output distributions. The target checks a whole tree of candidates in one forward pass, and coupled-noise match keeps the output exact at any temperature. Up to 6.8× fewer target passes and up to 3.4× the throughput of standard decoding on SDAR-8B Matches or beats calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget, at T = 0 and T = 1 The learned drafter transfers across six diffusion LMs New in v2, SPOT-Sets drafts whole commit sets for dynamic threshold decoding. Its exact mode keeps the threshold decoder's output and reaches 7.6× the throughput of standard decoding on SDAR-8B, against 5.0× for the threshold decoder alone (7.9× with max-commit) Code, drafters and a Colab demo are open. title: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding

details.title: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding
details.abstract: Image and video generators can produce spatially consistent visual content, but how to use this capability to improve spatial understanding remains underexplored. We study this problem from two perspectives: geometric supervision during training and explicit geometric evidence during inference. To this end, we introduce a unified geometric understanding and generation model (GeoUG) that integrates depth and multi-view generation with spatial understanding. First, we design a multi-scale depth codec that enables metric-depth generation using a pretrained visual autoencoder, and show that joint training yields task-dependent gains in spatial understanding. Second, we introduce 3DCueBench to control geometric difficulty while balancing selected 2D cues, and find that generated depth provides larger reasoning gains on questions requiring fine-grained geometric discrimination. Building on this finding, we develop adaptive interleaved reasoning, in which GeoUG first drafts an answer and then decides whether to generate geometric evidence to confirm or revise it. We train this decision through reinforcement learning, balancing accuracy gains over retaining the draft against generation cost. GeoUG achieves circular accuracies of 97.9%, 90.8%, and 94.2% on CV-Bench-3D, 3DCueBench, and DA-2K with fewer generation calls than always generating.

title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions

details.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
details.abstract: Can remembering more information actually make an LLM group worse at making decisions? In our new preprint, Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions , we investigate a fundamental question in multi-agent AI: what information should survive when a group's discussion is compressed into memory? Across four evaluated language models, we find that: Selecting relevant information can preserve misleading decoys. Prioritizing rare information is not consistently better than random selection. Facts attributed to multiple agents can receive undue weight, even when that apparent consensus provides no additional evidence. These findings suggest that better collective decision-making requires more than retrieving relevant information or preserving minority knowledge. How evidence is selected, represented, and attributed matters. We'd welcome feedback, alternative explanations, and discussion from researchers working on multi-agent systems, collective intelligence, and LLM memory.

At the harness level, each trajectory is distilled into a compact experience card containing the task context, initial conditions, and a strategy-level solution outline. These cards are stored in a persistent non-parametric memory, making newly acquired procedural knowledge immediately available to future tasks. At the model level, HaMo continually updates a single parameter-efficient adapter using selected trajectories together with historical replay, improving the model’s ability to exploit accumulated experience while preserving previously acquired capabilities.

title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving

details.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
details.abstract: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? The answer matters as formal verification must scale to keep up with frontier models producing research mathematics, yet new workflows rarely settle it, as their gains are often confounded with stronger models or more compute. We study this question with h1, a simple harness that gives a model an efficient interface to Lean 4 and keeps it working through verifier feedback and self-reflection, without imposing a decomposition or search structure. h1 reaches state-of-the-art results on PutnamBench, FATE-X, and FormalConjectures100-Solved, settles eight open problems in FormalConjectures, and, at matched models, matches or outperforms specialized workflows such as Goedel-Architect and AlphaProof Nexus, surprisingly showing that a single attempt (pass@1) can often scale to solve open problems. Through ablations and matched-model comparisons with Claude Code and AxProverBase, we find that simplicity alone is not enough: an efficient Lean interface largely determines cost and solve rate. We thus recommend that future work evaluate frontier models with efficient execution feedback before prescribing workflows, at the risk of bitter lessons.

title: PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds

details.title: PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds
details.abstract: Physical reasoning underpins how embodied systems understand and act in the physical world, yet vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable on questions about dynamics and physical causality. Progress is critically constrained by the scarcity of grounded counterfactual training data, as observational videos capture only the factual trajectory that occurred. The self-evolving paradigm offers a route beyond fixed datasets by enabling models to construct their own training problems. Extending this paradigm to physics, however, requires an external source of truth that can both validate model-proposed environments and verify alternative physical outcomes under intervention. We introduce \physevolve{}, a verifier-grounded self-evolving framework that trains VLMs for causal physical reasoning from model-proposed executable worlds and simulation-authored tasks. At each round, a shared VLM proposes executable world programs and evidence schemas; a deterministic physics engine freezes each valid world, simulates matched baseline and body-elided counterfactual branches, and synthesizes discrete, answer-bound visual tasks. Exact verifier feedback from task solving updates both the shared policy via GRPO and an adaptive curriculum over physical intents. Starting from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, \physevolve{} achieves targeted gains across PhysBench, CausalPhys, and ContPhy without human intervention data, improving PhysBench Throwing by $8.8$ points and ContPhy Counterfactual Removal and Goal-Pit by $7.4$ and $24.4$ points. These gains concentrate on interaction-sensitive and altered-world questions, demonstrating zero-shot transfer of causal principles to unseen complex dynamics (cloth, fluid, soft bodies) and real-world video.

title: DTCA: Denoising Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models

details.title: DTCA: Denoising Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models
details.abstract: Which tokens contribute most to a diffusion language model’s response? As tokens are revealed during denoising, they help shape predictions at the remaining masked positions. However, final-answer rewards provide little information about these individual contributions. People often prioritize major word classes such as nouns and verbs when thinking about a topic, and diffusion language models may show a similar pattern with different POS contributing unequally. DTCA thus derives POS-based token-level credit from confidence gains during denoising, so that learning signals reflect each token’s estimated contribution to the rest of the response.

title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success

details.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
details.abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (Huh et al, 2024) argues that as vision and language models scale, their representation spaces converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. The idea is that images and text are different projections of the same underlying world. As models recover that world more faithfully, they begin to agree on which inputs are similar. For example, if a vision model places two images close together in the representation space, a language model tends to place their captions close together too. In this work, we bring PRH to robotics and ask: can physical robot motion be viewed as another projection of that same world, such that more capable embodied models better align their vision and language representations with the structure of motion trajectories? Our evidence suggests the answer is yes. To test this, we use Sensorimotor Alignment (S²), which measures the overlap between neighborhoods of a model's sensory representations and neighborhoods of end-effector trajectories. Higher alignment means episodes nearby in sensory representation space are also nearby in motor representation space. Our first finding is that S² is positively related to downstream robot task success. We test a range of Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World Action Models (WAMs) in simulation, as well as policies on real robots. Across these settings, models with higher S² tend to achieve higher task success rates. This pattern provides empirical support for extending PRH to robotics. S² also explains, at the representation level, several phenomena that prior work has observed only through closed-loop results. For example, VLAs often ignore the language instruction and act mainly on what they see. We find that their task success correlates with the S² of their vision features, not their text features. In practice, S² can serve as a low-cost offline proxy for identifying which models are likely to achieve higher task success before closed-loop evaluation. For instance, it can identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly VLA fine-tuning.

title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving

details.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
details.abstract: DeepInfer recently open-sourced how DeepSeek manages the KV cache with 3FS and balances prefill and decode loads. Since some of those load balancers remain unreleased, they propose their own effective router, TAO—a tool-aware joint scheduling framework designed for bursty agentic workloads under tight KV cache budgets. Targeting agentic workloads that alternate between clustered GPUs and distributed CPU tools, TAO improves scheduling in three steps: Tool-Boundary Interruption: Pauses sessions during external tool calls to free up GPU capacity and places them into a shared waiting pool. Triplet Session Valuation: Scores each session–node pair without manual weight tuning by prioritizing time-decayed KV-cache credit, near-term tool-return readiness (predicted from runtime hints and historical tool durations), and token footprint. Joint DP Placement: Replaces greedy per-session routing with an asynchronous dynamic program (under 0.12% runtime overhead) that jointly selects and places waiting sessions under GPU capacity limits. Tested on DeepSeek-V4 Flash, Qwen3-32B, and GLM-4.7, TAO cuts latency by up to 26.8%, lowers mean TTFT by up to 36.3%, and boosts decode throughput by up to 29.5% over leading baselines.

title: TauIndianBankBench: Procedure-Aware, Action-Oriented Evaluation of Tool-Using Conversational Agents

details.title: TauIndianBankBench: Procedure-Aware, Action-Oriented Evaluation of Tool-Using Conversational Agents
details.abstract: Hi everyone, author here! 👋 Thanks for checking out TauIndianBankBench . TL;DR: Most agent benchmarks only check the final database state. But many required banking steps, like getting a closure quote before closing a deposit, don't change any records, so an agent can skip them and still be marked successful. TauIndianBankBench has 1,000 Indian retail-banking tasks with a simulated customer. It scores the outcome , and it also checks that the agent completed every required step and made no unrequested changes . With outcome-only scoring, 6.5–12.0% of sessions across all models were counted as successes even though the agent broke the procedure. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30161 📂 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/NPCI/tau-indian-banking 💻 Code: https://github.com/npci/TauIndianBankBench Contributions are welcome, whether that's new tasks, procedure fixes or additional banking flows. Feel free to open a PR on the dataset repo. You're also welcome to evaluate your own models and share the results. If you find this work useful, please upvote the paper and ❤️ like the dataset. It helps more people discover it! Happy to answer any questions! 🙏

title: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning

details.title: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning
details.abstract: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning Embodied planning requires more than knowing what to do. Agents must also understand when an action is executable and how it changes the world. We introduce CausGround , a non-parametric causal interaction grounding framework that distills interaction experience into reusable action preconditions and effects, enabling adaptive embodied planning without updating model parameters. What CausGround offers: Learning causal knowledge from experience: CausGround extracts action preconditions and effects from interaction trajectories, organizing them into reusable generic and instance-specific knowledge. Factorized world-state representation: Object attributes and inter-object relations are explicitly represented, enabling causal knowledge to be grounded in current visual observations. Task-grounded causal planning: CausGround reasons backward over action preconditions and forward over action effects, guiding a frozen MLLM planner toward executable multi-step actions. Improved embodied planning: Across VirtualHome and RoboCasa, CausGround improves average task success from 24.9% to 53.3% and closed-loop planning success from 43.0% to 57.0% , respectively. Generalization across environments: CausGround improves interaction reasoning on SWITCH (25.8% to 31.9%) and demonstrates real-world sequential robotic manipulation without parameter updates. Toward continuously adaptable embodied agents: As new interaction experience becomes available, CausGround provides a way to expand reusable causal knowledge without retraining the underlying MLLM. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29702 Project Page: https://causground.github.io/ Code: https://github.com/Intelligent-Interaction/CausGround

This repository provides Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct implementations of OFT-, GR00T-, and Pi-style policies that predict SONIC motion tokens and hand-control signals through a three-stage training pipeline: egocentric pre-training, humanoid adaptation, and downstream fine-tuning.

title: OmniSpectra: A Unified Foundation Model for Universal Spectra Representation Learning

details.title: OmniSpectra: A Unified Foundation Model for Universal Spectra Representation Learning
details.abstract: Hi everyone! Co-author here 👋 Spectra from different instruments sample the same wavelengths on very different pixel grids (up to 25× apart in our training corpus). Standard sequence models position tokens by pixel index, so the same line (e.g. Hα) gets a different positional code on every instrument. The usual fix is to resample everything onto a common grid, which blurs narrow lines. OmniSpectra is a wavelength-native masked autoencoder that removes this mismatch: Position = log λ, not pixel index. Tokens are anchored to physical wavelength. In log space, cosmological redshift becomes one uniform shift, which cancels in continuous RoPE, so attention depends on physical wavelength ratios rather than the detector grid. Resolution-gated Fourier decoder. Reconstructs flux at each instrument's native wavelengths. A gate set by the instrument's line-spread function suppresses detail the spectrograph cannot actually resolve. One set of weights, no resampling. Pretrained on 6.4M spectra from 8 surveys (SDSS, BOSS, eBOSS, SEGUE-1/2, DESI, APOGEE, GALAH). With only 12.2M parameters , it reaches state-of-the-art results across stellar parameters, galaxy properties, source classification and redshift, and outperforms much larger models such as AstroCLIP and AION-1. It is especially strong when labels are scarce. Pretrained on SDSS alone, it still transfers to APOGEE, whose near-infrared range it never saw during pretraining, with little degradation. Happy to answer questions!

title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching

details.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We’re excited to share IDM: Intrinsic Distribution Matching . Can a generator provide both the score supervision and the representation used for distribution matching? Building on internal DMD, IDM retains the full DMD correction and adds an explicit loss on the means and per-coordinate standard deviations of the generator’s own EMA features , without an external feature encoder. A Gaussian-plus-residual decomposition of the reverse-KL field motivates this additional moment constraint. At 2 NFE , IDM (Z-Image) achieves 94.25% on LongText-CN and 90.20% on LongText-EN , the best scores among the compared methods at this budget. Controlled ablations show consistent gains from the added moment loss, while generator EMA features perform competitively with DINOv2. We evaluate both Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B with full-parameter and LoRA tuning. Model weights: coming soon. If you find the work interesting, we’d appreciate a GitHub star ⭐ and an HF upvote!

title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs

details.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
details.abstract: LOWN (Look Only When Needed) is a training-free decoding method for diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) that processes the image only when a text-only prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Diffusion VLMs such as LLaDA-V process the whole image at every denoising step, but we find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average. Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step. Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs and cuts generation time by 57.4% on average.
